title: Drones Offer Central Asia an Escape From Foreign Dependency
gist: Central Asian states buying combat drones risk swapping long-standing Russian security dependency for a new dependency on Turkish suppliers such as Baykar; the author argues 2026 developments show local drone development and production is a viable alternative if regional politicians invest domestically.

themes.theme: Turkiye replacing Russia as security patron

insights.claim: Central Asian states may be replacing their long-term security dependency on Russia with a new dependency on Turkiye, as their drone deals concentrate on suppliers headquartered in a single country.
insights.speaker: Michael S. Coffey
insights.so_what: Turkish defense exporters (Baykar) are gaining a structural foothold in Central Asian procurement at Russia's expense; watch follow-on contracts and servicing deals.
insights.quote: The Central Asian states may just be replacing their long-term Russian security dependency with a Turkish one.
insights.locator: Drones are everywhere in the news

insights.claim: Concentrating drone procurement with foreign suppliers based in one state deepens dependency and worsens security vulnerabilities for Central Asian governments.
insights.speaker: Michael S. Coffey
insights.so_what: Single-supplier concentration is a supply-chain and political-leverage risk; diversification or localization would shift regional defense spending patterns.
insights.locator: Central Asian leaders risk deepening this dependency

insights.claim: Developments in 2026 indicate Central Asian states have real opportunities to develop and produce drones locally, which would benefit regional economies without offloading security responsibilities to foreign states.
insights.speaker: Michael S. Coffey
insights.so_what: A push toward indigenous drone manufacturing in Central Asia could create local defense-industrial and dual-use tech opportunities.
insights.quote: Local politicians just need to invest locally.

insights.claim: Drones have become ubiquitous on the frontlines of the Iran-U.S. War and the Russia-Ukraine War, and have now been used on a battlefield in Central Asia as well.
insights.speaker: Michael S. Coffey
insights.so_what: Battlefield drone proliferation into new theaters supports sustained demand for drone makers and counter-drone systems.
insights.locator: Drones are everywhere in the news
